topicName: Template Engine, Inheritance, Tags, and Filters
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Django Template Engine: Inheritance, Tags, and Filters"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django's template engine provides a powerful and expressive language for generating HTML dynamically. It separates Python logic from presentation design, ensuring clean and maintainable code. In this tutorial, we will explore advanced template concepts including layout inheritance, custom and built-in tags, and data manipulation using filters."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Template Inheritance"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Template inheritance allows you to create a base skeleton containing all common elements of your site (like headers, footers, and navigation bars) and define blocks that child templates can override."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":" {% block title %}My Django Site{% endblock %}
Site Navigation
{% block content %}{% endblock %}
"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To inherit from the base template and override specific blocks, child templates use the extends tag."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":" {% extends 'base.html %} {% block title %}Home Page{% endblock %} {% block content }}

Welcome to the Home Page

This content is injected into the base template.

{% endblock %}"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Working with Template Tags"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Template tags provide logic control within your HTML files. They can perform loops, evaluate conditions, load static files, and handle URL routing."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Conditional Logic: Use {% if condition %} ... {% elif %} ... {% else %} ... {% endif %} to render elements conditionally."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Iteration: Use {% for item in list %} ... {% empty %} ... {% endfor %} to loop through querysets or lists."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"URL Resolution: Use {% url 'view_name' param %} to dynamically generate safe URLs."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"{% if user.is_authenticated %}

Hello, {{ user.username }}!

Logout {% else %} Login {% endif %}"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Transforming Data with Filters"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Filters are used to modify variables before they are displayed in the template. They are denoted by a pipe symbol (|) and can take optional arguments."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":" {{ title|lower }} {{ long_description|truncatechars:50 }} {{ bio|default:"No bio provided." }}"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Django Templates"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep business logic out of templates; process data thoroughly in views or models before passing them to the context."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always organize your templates inside an app-specific folder (e.g., templates/app_name/) to avoid naming collisions."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Utilize the load static tag at the top of templates that require CSS, JavaScript, or images."}]
